title: Radiator Replacement
summary: Blueprint for confirming radiator leaks, restriction, or cooling-system damage before quoting replacement.
symptoms: Coolant leak from radiator tanks, seams, or core
Overheating at idle, in traffic, or under load
Coolant smell near the front of the vehicle
Visible corrosion, damaged fins, or pressure-test failure
inspect_first: Cooling fan operation and airflow through the condenser/radiator stack
likely_causes: Cracked plastic tank or radiator seam leak
Cooling fan or thermostat issue blamed on the radiator
repair_overview: Confirm radiator failure before draining the system.
Remove shrouds, hoses, cooler lines, and mounts as needed.
Transfer brackets or sensors, install the radiator, and secure hoses.
Refill coolant, bleed air, pressure test, and verify fan operation.
common_mistakes: Replacing the radiator without finding why the vehicle overheated
Forgetting transmission cooler line sealing checks where equipped
Missing a weak cap, hose, thermostat, or fan fault
estimate_guidance: Include coolant, bleed time, and any required hose or cap recommendations.
Add labor for tight front-end packaging, seized lower mounts, or cooler lines.
Warn customers that prior overheating can reveal additional issues after repair.

recommended_repairs.title: Thermostat Inspection
recommended_repairs.description: Commonly checked when temperature control, not the radiator, may be the main fault.

recommended_repairs.title: Radiator Hose Inspection
recommended_repairs.description: Mechanics often inspect hoses and clamps while the radiator is already drained.

recommended_repairs.title: Coolant Service
recommended_repairs.description: Related fluid check when coolant age, contamination, or refill quality affects the repair.

diagnostic_context.intro: Radiator replacement should follow pressure-test evidence or clear restriction/heat-exchange failure.
